title: The First Triumvirate
objective: After this level you can explain the informal alliance of Caesar, Pompey and Crassus.
summary: In 60 BCE Caesar, Pompey and Crassus pooled their power. Julia’s death in 54 BCE and Crassus’s at Carrhae in 53 BCE broke it apart.

cards.headline: Three ambitious men agreed to share Rome. It couldn’t last.
A private deal
cards.body: In 60 BCE Julius Caesar, Pompey and Crassus formed an informal alliance, later called the First Triumvirate. Each gained something the Senate had refused him: Caesar a consulship, Pompey land for his veterans, and Crassus favors for his allies. Pompey married Caesar’s daughter Julia to seal it.

cards.headline: Falling apart
cards.body: Julia died in 54 BCE, weakening the bond between her husband and her father. Then Crassus, the richest man in Rome and the victor over Spartacus, was killed in 53 BCE after a disastrous defeat by the Parthians at Carrhae. Only two rivals were left.

cards.fact: Pompey married Caesar’s daughter Julia to seal the alliance.
cards.context: Her death in 54 BCE removed the family tie between the two most powerful men in Rome.

options.label: The Senate dissolved it by law

Julia and Crassus died, leaving two rivals
